items.title: Alcide "Slow Drag" Pavageau and Lawrence Marrero Interview, 1957-09-01
items.q: Yeah, that's where George come got me from. The first recording we made was Gene, William.

ctx.x: You're barring all four strings with that first finger, are you? Yeah, that's right. And what are you doing with the second finger?

Yeah, the second finger, two and barring all three of them. Barring three? Yeah. And then, you see, of course I know we can't do it all night, but I would like to show you how to make right from there to jump in your seventh chord. Man, them boys play something. Man, sure. Who was that Bill Huntington? Huntington and then John Schaff. That's true. No. Man, the boys play something bad. But Bill is more of a jazz band you play than Bill, or Schaff is, but Schaff is, no more music, is it? He said, I'm going to run,…
Yeah, I didn't know. I thought you were working in the furniture. No, not that time, no.

items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-12-09
items.q: Not used to playing hymns. Uh... You got a Lawrence. Uh... Banjo.

ctx.x: Everybody accepted it. And, uh... Some of them was playing, some of the fellas didn't even know. You see? Cause you'd take, like... Piano player. Elder Poinnelly.

Not used to playing hymns. Uh... You got a Lawrence. Uh... Banjo. Uh... for the congregation of the church. And then I met on my last mother that died and I changed my pastoral instance and I met some nuns. We call them sisters, y'all. We call them sisters. Two of them had a youth period of the church. I lived there with Doug, Plotty Jack and some of them. And then I was going to go to Europe. These two young people invited me to come to the church. And then they would come to get me. So, sure enough, they came…
Where was that? I was just out of Cincinnati.
